title: DMCC Speciality Chemicals Ltd - 506405 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose to INR 177 crore from INR 150 crore QoQ, mostly raw-material pass-through; FY26 revenue INR 582 crore.
summary.overview: Management attributed the quarter's sharp top-line rise to pass-through of higher sulfur and boron raw-material prices rather than volume, and said absolute margins were maintained though percentage margins fell. Sulfur supply was constrained by Middle East/Hormuz disruption, and the Roha plant ran at about 60% capacity for roughly 15 days in March before supply was restored. Working capital and short-term borrowings rose substantially on higher inventory, debtor and advance-payment requirements for boron, at about 8.75-9% interest. Management declined to give quantified guidance beyond saying FY27 specialty utilisation should be better than FY26.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR 150 crore in the previous quarter (QoQ)
described as one of the highest top lines in the company

financial_highlights.metric: Interest rate on incremental working capital lines

financial_highlights.change: described as well within industry norms

segments.name: Sulfur / sulfuric acid (bulk chemicals)
segments.commentary: Dahej running at about 95% capacity per management; Roha slowed to about 60% for roughly 15 days in March due to imported sulfur shortage. Each site keeps about 15-20 days (about 1,500 tons) of sulfur inventory. Both plants have roughly 350 tons per day sulfuric acid capacity.

segments.name: Boron chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 H1 output was lost due to boron ore supply disruption from Turkey; plants were back at full capacity in H2 with adequate stock now. Company moved from credit purchases to paying advances with 90-120 day supply lead times, raising working capital.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Europe business declining; growth in Latin America (replacing most lost European volume), with sales to China and Japan. Specialty portfolio is below management's 50% target; the company reports a single segment only.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to project FY27 utilisation, calling the situation too volatile; said it expects specialty capacity utilisation to be better than FY25-26.
Plants currently operating at capacity with no restriction, per management, but situation described as highly dynamic.
Supply chain would take a few months to normalise even if Strait of Hormuz reopens; prices expected to keep rising until supply eases.
Management does not expect boron/borax distressed selling to continue, though overall non-boric demand is lower until gas supply normalises in Morbi and other ceramic/glass centres.
Long-term target: specialty portfolio at least 50% of revenue; previous mix was about 30% commodities and 60-70% bulk chemicals at name change.
capex_capacity: Dahej expansion undertaken earlier to increase manufacturing footprint and sulfuric acid volumes.
Roha plant reduced to about 60% capacity in March 2026 due to imported sulfur unavailability; now back to normal.
Some specialty products in boron and an enhanced-oil-recovery polymer product have started commercial sales; no volume or margin projections given.
Research pipeline: several specialties expected to reach commercial stage in FY27 or FY28, unquantified.

Land parcel near Ambernath (Nalimbi), declared forest land; Supreme Court ruled in company's favour but Maharashtra government has not transferred title, so monetisation is blocked. Proceeds could go to capex or debt reduction.
demand_pricing: Sulfur supply remains short; prices at all-time highs, partly from new Indonesian nickel smelter demand (about 3 million tons) before the war and then Hormuz disruption.
Specialty pricing passed through with a lag because contracts are quarterly and negotiated in advance; margins expected to average out over time.
Non-boric borax/frit demand weak in Morbi and similar centres due to gas shortages and customer stock liquidation, causing glut and distressed pricing.
Chinese sulfuric acid export restrictions; management sees customers seeking diversification away from China, but no significant single order won yet.
Sulfuric acid is low margin; company limited by specialty market access, not production, so it does not prioritise sulfuric acid sales over captive use.

qa_highlights.question: How much did Roha's disruption cost in volume or revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Roha was slowed to about 60% capacity for roughly 15 days in March rather than shut down, as imports were unavailable; no quantification given. Dahej has domestic sulfur sourcing.

qa_highlights.question: What interest rate and when does working capital ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental lines cost about 8.75-9%; the issue is absolute quantum, not rate, driven by higher stock values, debtors and boron advances. No date given for easing.

qa_highlights.question: Latin America progress and pass-through of raw-material inflation in specialty?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says most lost European business has been replaced by Latin American business; Japan, Korea and China are being explored. Specialty prices pass through with a lag due to quarterly contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Ambernath land monetisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Land is actually near Ambernath at Nalimbi, forest land with a favourable Supreme Court order, but state has not transferred title, so no monetisation yet; options being examined.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company report specialty vs bulk margins separately, and when is it a true specialty company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will keep reporting a single chemicals segment, saying the split would be subjective; it considers 50% specialty share the right threshold for a specialty identity.

qa_highlights.question: R&D intensity and plans?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is mainly process development and largely people cost; management said plans to increase R&D spend will show in coming quarters, with no figures given.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 utilisation and sulfur inventory cost?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 projection given; sulfur inventory kept at 15-20 days (about 1,500 tons per site); management did not disclose purchase or current sulfur prices.

risks_watch: Sulfur availability and price: Hormuz disruption; supply may take months to normalise even after reopening.
Working capital and short-term borrowing build-up; interest cost rising on the larger absolute debt.
Roha dependence on imported sulfur; utilisation may fall again if imports stay unavailable.
Non-boric borax and frit demand weak until gas supply in consuming centres normalises.
Europe specialty business shrinking; replacement depends on Latin America, Japan, Korea and China developments.
Low specialty share versus 50% target, and limited R&D spend, questioned by analysts.
Ambernath/Nalimbi land monetisation timing depends on state government title transfer.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on near-term visibility: management repeatedly declined to give forward projections, citing volatility. Confident about supply recovery and pricing pass-through at a qualitative level, but evasive on quantification of disruption, margins by product and R&D plans.
key_quotes: We will continue to report a single segment.
It's really my style not to give futuristic projections.

growth.why: No quantified FY27 growth guidance; management only said specialty utilisation should be better than FY25-26, with Q4 revenue rise (177 vs 150 crore QoQ) driven mainly by raw-material pass-through rather than volume.
